In $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$, the rows are in arithmetic progression with $R_3 - R_2 = R_2 - R_1 = [3, 3, 3]$, making the rows linearly dependent and $\det(A) = 0$. questions.question_text:
Consider a system that uses 5 bits for representing signed integers in 2’s complement
format. In this system, two integers 𝐴 and 𝐵 are represented as 𝐴=01010 and
𝐵=11010. Which one of the following operations will result in either an arithmetic
overflow or an arithmetic underflow?
questions.subtopic: Number representations and computer arithmetic (fixed and floating point)
questions.explaination: In a 5-bit 2's complement representation, the range is $[-2^4, 2^4 - 1] = [-16, +15]$. Here, $A = 01010_2 = +10$ and $B = 11010_2 = -6$. The operation $A - B = 10 - (-6) = +16$, which exceeds $+15$, resulting in an arithmetic overflow.

In this system, two integers $A$ and $B$ are represented as $A = 01010$ and $B = 11010$. questions.question_text:
Consider a permutation sampled uniformly at random from the set of all
permutations of {1, 2, 3, ⋯, 𝑛} for some 𝑛 ≥4. Let 𝑋 be the event that 1 occurs
before 2 in the permutation, and 𝑌 the event that 3 occurs before 4. Which one of
the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: The events 𝑋 and 𝑌 are mutually exclusive
options.B: The events 𝑋 and 𝑌 are independent
options.C: Either event 𝑋 or 𝑌 must occur
options.D: Event 𝑋 is more likely than event 𝑌

questions.explaination: By symmetry in random permutations of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, $P(X) = P(1 \text{ before } 2) = 1/2$, and $P(Y) = P(3 \text{ before } 4) = 1/2$. Because the relative order of the disjoint pair $\{1, 2\}$ has no bearing on the relative order of $\{3, 4\}$, the joint probability is $P(X \cap Y) = 1/4 = P(X)P(Y)$, proving that $X$ and $Y$ are independent.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a permutation sampled uniformly at random from the set of all permutations of $\{1, 2, 3, \dots, n\}$ for some $n \ge 4$. Let $X$ be the event that 1 occurs before 2 in the permutation, and $Y$ the event that 3 occurs before 4. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options_latex.A: The events $X$ and $Y$ are mutually exclusive
options_latex.D: Event $X$ is more likely than event $Y$

options.A:
In the cycle stealing mode of DMA, one word of data is transferred between an I/O
device and main memory in a stolen cycle
options.B:
For bulk data transfer, the burst mode of DMA has a higher throughput than the
cycle stealing mode
options.C:
Programmed I/O mechanism has a better CPU utilization than the interrupt driven
I/O mechanism
options.D:
The CPU can start executing an interrupt service routine faster with vectored
interrupts than with non-vectored interrupts

questions.subtopic: I/O interface: interrupt and DMA mode
questions.explaination: Programmed I/O requires the CPU to stay in a busy-waiting polling loop to check device readiness, wasting processor cycles and yielding poor CPU utilization. Interrupt-driven I/O frees the CPU to execute other tasks while I/O operations are underway, providing significantly better CPU utilization. Thus, statement (C) is FALSE.

questions.question_text:
A user starts browsing a webpage hosted at a remote server. The browser opens a
single TCP connection to fetch the entire webpage from the server. The webpage
consists of a top-level index page with multiple embedded image objects. Assume
that all caches (e.g., DNS cache, browser cache) are all initially empty. The
following packets leave the user’s computer in some order.
(i)
HTTP GET request for the index page
(ii)
DNS request to resolve the web server’s name to its IP address
(iii)
HTTP GET request for an image object
(iv)
TCP SYN to open a connection to the web server
Which one of the following is the CORRECT chronological order (earliest in time
to latest) of the packets leaving the computer ?
questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks
questions.explaination: Initially all caches are empty. The client must first send a DNS query (ii) to resolve the server hostname to an IP. Next, it establishes a TCP connection by sending TCP SYN (iv). Once connected, it sends an HTTP GET request for the index HTML page (i). After parsing the HTML and identifying embedded images, it sends HTTP GET requests for the images (iii).

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about a relation R in first normal form (1NF)
is/are TRUE ?

options.A: R can have a multi-attribute key
options.B: R cannot have a foreign key
options.C: R cannot have a composite attribute
options.D: R cannot have more than one candidate key

questions.explaination: A relation is in 1NF if and only if all attribute values are atomic, which explicitly forbids composite or multi-valued attributes (making (C) TRUE). 1NF places no limitation on candidate keys having multiple attributes (multi-attribute keys are fully permitted, making (A) TRUE) or the presence of foreign keys.

Let 𝐿1, 𝐿2 be two regular languages and 𝐿3 a language which is not regular.
Which of the following statements is/are always TRUE?

options.A: 𝐿1 = 𝐿2 if and only if 𝐿1 ∩ 𝐿2̅̅̅ = 𝜙

questions.subtopic: Regular and context-free languages, pumping lemma
questions.explaination: Regular languages are closed under complementation and union; since $L_1, L_2$ are regular, $\overline{L_1}$ and $\overline{L_2}$ are regular, so $\overline{L_1} \cup \overline{L_2}$ is regular (D is TRUE). If $L_3$ is non-regular, its complement $\overline{L_3}$ must also be non-regular, because if $\overline{L_3}$ were regular, its complement $\overline{\overline{L_3}} = L_3$ would be regular, a contradiction (C is TRUE).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about threads is/are TRUE?

options.A: Threads can only be implemented in kernel space
options.B: Each thread has its own file descriptor table for open files
options.C: All the threads belonging to a process share a common stack
options.D: Threads belonging to a process are by default not protected from each other

questions.subtopic: System calls, processes, threads, inter-process communication
questions.explaination: All threads of a single process share the same address space (code, global data, heap) and open files. Because they run within the same virtual address space without memory protection barriers between them, one thread can corrupt another thread's memory; hence they are by default not protected from each other (D is TRUE). Each thread maintains its own private stack and registers.

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐴 and 𝐵 be two events in a probability space with 𝑃(𝐴) = 0.3, 𝑃(𝐵) = 0.5,
and 𝑃(𝐴∩𝐵) = 0.1. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

options.A: The two events 𝐴 and 𝐵 are independent
options.C: 𝑃(𝐴∩𝐵𝑐) = 0.2, where 𝐵𝑐 is the complement of the event 𝐵
options.D:
𝑃(𝐴𝑐∩𝐵𝑐) = 0.4, where 𝐴𝑐 and 𝐵𝑐 are the complements of the events 𝐴 and 𝐵,
respectively

questions.explaination: We are given $P(A) = 0.3$, $P(B) = 0.5$, and $P(A \cap B) = 0.1$. First, $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = 0.3 + 0.5 - 0.1 = 0.7$ (B is TRUE). Second, $P(A \cap B^c) = P(A) - P(A \cap B) = 0.3 - 0.1 = 0.2$ (C is TRUE). Since $P(A)P(B) = 0.15 \neq 0.1$, the events are not independent.

options_latex.C: $P(A \cap B^c) = 0.2$, where $B^c$ is the complement of the event $B$
options_latex.D: $P(A^c \cap B^c) = 0.4$, where $A^c$ and $B^c$ are the complements of the events $A$ and $B$, respectively

Consider the circuit shown below where the gates may have propagation delays.
Assume that all signal transitions occur instantaneously and that wires have no
delays. Which of the following statements about the circuit is/are CORRECT?

options.A: With no propagation delays, the output 𝒀 is always logic Zero
options.B: With no propagation delays, the output 𝒀 is always logic One
options.C:
With propagation delays, the output 𝒀 can have a transient logic One after 𝑿
transitions from logic Zero to logic One
options.D:
With propagation delays, the output 𝒀 can have a transient logic Zero after 𝑿
transitions from logic One to logic Zero

questions.explaination: The circuit computes $Y = X \cdot \overline{X}$. In steady-state with no gate delays, $X \cdot \overline{X} = 0$, so $Y$ is always logic Zero (A is TRUE). When $X$ transitions from 0 to 1, if the inverter has a non-zero propagation delay, both inputs to the AND gate remain logic 1 for the duration of the inverter delay, producing a transient logic 1 glitch (C is TRUE).

TCP client P successfully establishes a connection to TCP server Q. Let 𝑁𝑃 denote
the sequence number in the SYN sent from P to Q. Let 𝑁𝑄 denote the
acknowledgement number in the SYN ACK from Q to P. Which of the following
statements is/are CORRECT?

options.A: The sequence number 𝑁𝑃 is chosen randomly by P
options.B: The sequence number 𝑁𝑃 is always 0 for a new connection
options.C: The acknowledgement number 𝑁𝑄 is equal to 𝑁𝑃
options.D: The acknowledgement number 𝑁𝑄 is equal to 𝑁𝑃+ 1

questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: During TCP connection establishment, the initial sequence number $N_P$ is chosen pseudo-randomly to avoid cross-connection packet collisions and mitigate spoofing attacks (A is TRUE). Because a SYN packet consumes exactly 1 sequence number in the sequence space, server $Q$ acknowledges it with $N_Q = N_P + 1$ (D is TRUE).

Consider a 5-stage pipelined processor with Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction
Decode (ID), Execute (EX), Memory Access (MEM), and Register Writeback (WB)
stages. Which of the following statements about forwarding is/are CORRECT?

options.A:
In a pipelined execution, forwarding means the result from a source stage of an
earlier instruction is passed on to the destination stage of a later instruction
options.B:
In forwarding, data from the output of the MEM stage can be passed on to the
input of the EX stage of the next instruction
options.C: Forwarding cannot prevent all pipeline stalls
options.D:
Forwarding does not require any extra hardware to retrieve the data from the
pipeline stages

questions.explaination: Forwarding (bypassing) routes intermediate results directly from pipeline registers of an earlier instruction to execution inputs of a subsequent instruction (A is TRUE). While forwarding resolves many ALU data dependencies without stalls, it cannot prevent a load-use stall (where the loaded data is needed immediately in the subsequent instruction's EX stage), requiring at least one stall cycle (C is TRUE).

Let 𝐴 and 𝐵 be non-empty finite sets such that there exist one-to-one and onto
functions (i) from 𝐴 to 𝐵 and (ii) from 𝐴× 𝐴 to 𝐴∪𝐵. The number of possible
values of |𝐴| is __________
questions.subtopic: Sets, relations, functions, partial orders and lattices
questions.explaination: A bijection from $A$ to $B$ implies $|A| = |B| = n$. A bijection from $A \times A$ to $A \cup B$ implies $|A \times A| = |A \cup B|$. We have $|A \times A| = n^2$, and $n \le |A \cup B| \le 2n$. Thus $n \le n^2 \le 2n$. Since $A$ is non-empty ($n \ge 1$), dividing by $n$ gives $1 \le n \le 2$. This allows exactly two integer solutions: $n = 1$ (where $A = B$) and $n = 2$ (where $A \cap B = \emptyset$).

The value of the expression 3 + 1 + 5 ∗2 / 7 + 2 −4 −7 −6 / 2 as per the

questions.explaination: Precedence order is $+$ (highest, left-associative), then $-$ (right-associative), then $*$ (right-associative), then $/$ (lowest, right-associative). Evaluating $+$ first: $3+1+5 = 9$ and $7+2 = 9$. Expression becomes $9 * 2 / 9 - 4 - 7 - 6 / 2$. Evaluating $-$ right-associatively: $4 - (7 - 6) = 4 - 1 = 3$, giving $9 - 3 = 6$. The expression becomes $9 * 2 / 6 / 2$. Next $*$ gives $18 / 6 / 2$. Evaluating $/$ right-associatively: $6 / 2 = 3$, and $18 / 3 = 6$.

and D is _________
